include: Trades futures (index / metals / rates) with a public, checkable track record: audited competition results (e.g. Robbins World Cup), regulated prop/CTA history, published books with testable rules, or long-running live-trading content
Concept can be written as objective rules (entry, stop, target) that a computer can test
Teaches process and risk, not lifestyle
exclude_red_flags: Signals or copy-trading groups as the main product
Rules that change after the fact ('it was a valid setup in hindsight')
selection_criteria.note: Credentials below were checked against public secondary sources where possible; items marked (unverified) could not be confirmed from a primary source. Mechanizations are this lab's interpretation, not the trader's exact method.

concepts.name: Liquidity Sweep + Rejection Block + FVG
concepts.short: Your playbook: stop-run of a liquidity pool, rejection wick, enter the displacement FVG at 50%.

source.trader: Your plan (ICT-style terminology; order-flow scalpers such as Fabio Valentini describe the same liquidity-grab idea)
source.channel: Concept family — ICT vocabulary, mechanized here
credibility_evidence: Liquidity-grab / failed-auction reversals are a long-standing idea in auction-market and order-flow trading
Rules here are fully objective, so the result is a test of the idea, not of any personality
guru_flags: The FVG / 'rejection block' vocabulary comes from ICT, whose results are not audited
Most YouTube content on it is discretionary and judged in hindsight

concepts.summary: Mark resting liquidity (swing highs/lows, prior-day high/low, overnight high/low). Wait for a bar to trade through a pool and close back inside with a long rejection wick (the rejection block). Then require a displacement fair value gap in the reversal direction and enter on the retrace into the FVG. Stop beyond the sweep extreme, target fixed 2R.

rules.context: NY AM 09:30-11:30 ET. Pools: 3-bar pivots (≤300 bars old), prior RTH day high/low (if not already run overnight), overnight high/low.
rules.entry: Sweep bar closes back inside the pool with wick ≥ 40% of its range. Within 10 bars a 3-candle FVG forms in the reversal direction (size ≥ 0.1×ATR). Limit order at the FVG midpoint (CE).
rules.management: None (set and forget). Optional break-even at 1R via --be.
rules.filters: FVG respected: cancel if a bar closes through the FVG's far edge. Order expires after 20 bars. Max 2 trades/day; flat by 15:55 ET; skip stops > 3×ATR.

concepts.notes: The benchmark the other concepts are compared to.

concepts.name: Turtle Soup (false breakout of a 20-bar extreme)
concepts.short: Fade a fresh 20-bar high/low that fails — the original codified liquidity sweep.

source.channel: Interviews / talks on YouTube (e.g. Chat With Traders, Complete Traders Edge 'Greatest Traders' episode)
credibility_evidence: Profiled in Jack Schwager's 'The New Market Wizards' (1992)
Co-authored 'Street Smarts' (1995) with Laurence Connors, where Turtle Soup is published with exact rules
Decades as a professional futures trader / CTA

concepts.summary: When price makes a new 20-bar low but the previous 20-bar low is at least 4 bars old, buy back above the old low; mirror for shorts. It's a liquidity sweep defined purely mechanically, without FVG confirmation.

rules.context: NY AM 09:30-11:30 ET, intraday adaptation of the daily original.
rules.entry: Bar breaks the prior 20-bar low (that low ≥4 bars old) → buy-stop 1 tick above the old low, valid 3 bars.
rules.target: Fixed 2R (the original trails; your plan fixes 2R).
rules.filters: Cancel if the stop trades before the fill.

concepts.notes: Strong control for your playbook: if Turtle Soup matches LSRB-FVG, the FVG/rejection filters add little.

concepts.name: "Oops" — open outside yesterday's range, reclaim
concepts.short: RTH opens beyond the prior day's high/low and trades back inside: trapped gap traders.

credibility_evidence: Won the 1987 Robbins World Cup Championship of Futures Trading (widely reported +11,000%)
Pattern published in his books with explicit rules
guru_flags: Sells courses and newsletters (author-educator, but the record predates it)

concepts.summary: If the RTH session opens below the prior day's low and then trades back above it, buy (mirror for shorts). Stop under the session low so far.

rules.entry: Open < PDL and a 5m bar closes back above PDL → market entry next bar.
rules.stop: 2 ticks beyond the RTH low (high) so far.
rules.filters: Only on gap-outside-range days, so it trades rarely.

concepts.notes: Low frequency: needs a long history for a meaningful sample.

concepts.name: Opening-range breakout failure
concepts.short: First 15-minute range breaks, then fails: fade the trapped breakout traders.

source.trader: Al Brooks (failed breakouts) / Toby Crabel (opening range)
credibility_evidence: Al Brooks: long-time E-mini day trader, author of the Wiley price-action trilogy
Toby Crabel: 'Day Trading with Short Term Price Patterns and Opening Range Breakout' (1990), later ran a fund
guru_flags: Brooks sells a course; his record is not publicly audited

concepts.summary: Mark the 09:30-09:45 range. If a bar trades beyond it and closes back inside, enter in the opposite direction; stop beyond the session extreme.

rules.context: 09:45-11:30 ET, first failure of the day only.
rules.entry: Bar high > OR high and close < OR high → short at market next bar (mirror for long).
rules.stop: 2 ticks beyond the RTH high/low so far.

concepts.name: Session-liquidity sweep & reclaim (Asia / London / overnight)
concepts.short: NY open runs the Asia, London or overnight extreme and rejects it.

source.trader: Fabio Valentini (NQ order-flow scalper) and similar session-liquidity traders
source.channel: Podcast and interview appearances on YouTube
credibility_evidence: Reported multiple top placings in the Robbins World Cup (exact figures vary by source — unverified)
Trades NQ in the NY session with auction-market / order-flow tools
guru_flags: Co-founder of an order-flow software product (commercial interest)
His real edge is read from order flow (footprint, CVD), which OHLC bars can't fully capture

concepts.summary: Pre-mark the Asia (20:00-24:00 ET), London (02:00-05:00 ET) and full overnight highs/lows. In the NY AM, when a bar runs one of them and closes back inside with a rejection wick, take the reversal.

rules.entry: Bar trades through a session extreme, closes back inside, wick ≥ 40% of range → market entry next bar.
rules.stop: 2 ticks beyond the sweep bar extreme.
rules.filters: Each level can be used once per day; a level broken without rejection is spent.

concepts.notes: Your playbook without the FVG step — shows whether the FVG improves the entry.

concepts.name: Inventory Retracement Bar (IRB)
concepts.short: Trend continuation off a bar with a ≥45% counter-trend wick.

credibility_evidence: Cited with 30+ real-money trading competition wins (count varies by source and year)
Featured in Technical Analysis of Stocks & Commodities (V.34:08)

concepts.summary: In a trend (20 EMA sloping strongly), find a bar that retraces ≥45% of its range against the trend (institutional inventory being worked). Buy a break of its high; stop under its low.

rules.context: 09:45-15:00 ET; 20 EMA slope over 5 bars ≥ 0.15 ATR/bar; bar entirely on the trend side of the EMA.
rules.entry: Buy-stop 1 tick above the IRB high (sell-stop below for shorts), valid 5 bars.
rules.stop: 1 tick beyond the IRB's other extreme.
rules.filters: Cancel if the stop trades before the fill.

concepts.notes: Opposite logic to your playbook (continuation, not reversal), a useful diversifier.

concepts.name: Value-area re-entry (Market Profile 80% rule)
concepts.short: Open outside yesterday's value, get accepted back inside → rotate through value.

source.trader: James Dalton (Market Profile); taught on YouTube by auction-market traders such as Tom Dante
credibility_evidence: Dalton co-authored 'Mind Over Markets' and 'Markets in Profile', the standard Market Profile texts
Auction-market theory is used on professional futures desks
guru_flags: The '80%' figure is folklore, not a measured statistic: test it

concepts.summary: Build yesterday's RTH volume profile (70% value area). If today opens outside value and price closes back inside value for 30 minutes, trade toward the far side of value.

rules.entry: RTH open above VAH (below VAL) and 30 consecutive minutes of closes inside value → market entry toward the opposite side.
rules.stop: 2 ticks beyond the RTH extreme so far.
rules.target: Fixed 2R (classic target is the opposite VA edge).
rules.filters: One signal per day. Value area here is approximated from OHLCV bars (no tick data).

concepts.name: VWAP ±2σ band sweep & reclaim
concepts.short: Day high/low runs outside the 2σ VWAP band, then closes back inside.

source.trader: Auction / order-flow prop desks (e.g. Axia Futures free webinars); loose attribution
credibility_evidence: Axia operates an FCA-regulated proprietary trading arm in London
VWAP is the standard institutional execution benchmark
guru_flags: This exact rule set is our mechanization, not a published Axia strategy

concepts.summary: Session VWAP with volume-weighted standard-deviation bands. When a bar makes a new session low below the -2σ band and closes back above the band, buy; mirror for shorts.

rules.entry: New RTH low, low < VWAP-2σ, close > VWAP-2σ → market entry next bar.

concepts.name: Al Brooks H2 / L2 second entry
concepts.short: With-trend pullback to the 20 EMA; take the second attempt to resume.

credibility_evidence: Decades of E-mini day trading; author of the Wiley price-action trilogy
guru_flags: Sells a course; record not publicly audited
Highly discretionary: the mechanized version is a simplification

concepts.summary: In a trend (price above a rising 20 EMA), count pullback legs. The second time a bar trades above the prior bar's high (H2) after the pullback touched the EMA, buy above a strong bull signal bar. L2 is the mirror.

rules.entry: H2 signal bar (bull close in the top 40%) → buy-stop 1 tick above, valid 1 bar.
rules.target: Fixed 2R (Brooks often scalps 1R; your plan fixes 2R).
rules.filters: Pullback must touch within 0.25 ATR of the EMA; resets on a new trend extreme.
